meta.title: Learning by example 动物学习

blocks.html:
READING PASSAGE 1

Read the passage and answer Questions 1–13.

Learning by example

evidence from studies of rats and birds

A The best known model of animal learning behaviour is probably the so-called classical model associated with the Russian scientist Pavlov. The key features of this model are stimulus, outcome and repetition. Pavlov demonstrated that animals could be trained to associate a sensory stimulus with a particular outcome, even where no natural association exists. In one famous experiment, dogs learned to associate the sound of a bell with the expectation of food. Subsequent models, such as the ‘operant conditioning’ model, also involved observing animals in isolation. Recently, however, behavioural research has focused on how animals are equipped to learn in social settings. And interest in the concept of role modelling, already a popular notion for guiding child development, has spread to other species.

B Heyes and Galef (1996) have compiled some very interesting and accessible papers on social learning in mammals. One of these papers starts with an account of a school field trip to Israel. In a pine forest there, many pine cones were discovered which had been stripped to the central core. So an investigation was started which had no weighty theoretical intent, but was directed initially at finding out what were eating the nutritious pine seeds, and how they managed to get them out of the cones. The culprit proved to be the versatile and athletic black rat. The forest-dwelling rat used a standard technique, biting off each cone scale in sequence, from base to tip, following the spiral growth pattern of the cone.

C The investigation was then broadened, with the aim of determining how the rat acquires such a skill. Urban black rats were found to lack the skill, and were unable to learn it even when they were housed with experienced cone strippers, such as those found in Israel. However, infants of urban mothers who were fostered to forest mothers acquired the skill, whereas infants of forest mothers fostered by urban mothers did not. Clearly, the skill is not inherited, but has to be taught.

D Further elegant experiments showed that naive adult urban rats can develop the skill if they are provided with cones from which the first complete spiral of scales have been removed, rather as people can deduce how to use a new photocopier once they have been shown how to switch it on. In the case of forest rats, mothers supply their infants with cones which they have partially stripped, thereby providing the key for acquiring the complete stripping skill.

E We might conclude that this is a good example of adaptive learning, but how economical is it? The researchers went on to determine this by measuring the oxygen uptake of a rat stripping a cone. The rat was placed in a metabolic chamber so that the amount of energy used in the cone-stripping operation could be calculated. This was then compared with the energy benefit of the pine seeds, as measured by a machine known as a calorimeter. The rat's energy expenditure proved to be less than 10% of the energetic value of the cone – an acceptable profit margin.

F A paper by Bednekoff and Balda (1996) provides another example of the adaptiveness of social learning, this time in birds. It concerns the seed caching behaviour of two birds: Clark's Nutcracker (Nucifraga columbiana) and the Mexican Jay (Aphelocoma ultramarina). The former is a specialist, caching 30,000 or so seeds in scattered locations, from where it recovers them over the winter months. The Mexican Jay also caches food, but is not nearly as dependent on this as the Nutcracker. The two species also differ in their social structure, the Nutcracker being rather solitary, while the Jay forages in social groups.

G An experiment was conducted to discover not just whether a bird can remember where it hid a seed itself, but also if it can remember where it saw another bird hide a seed. The design of the experiment is slightly comical, with a cacher bird wandering about a room with lots of holes in the floor and hiding food in some of them, while watched by an observer bird perched in a cage. Two days later, cachers and observers are tested for their discovery rate against an estimated random performance. In the role of cacher, not only the Nutcracker but also the less specialised Jay performed above the rate of chance. More surprisingly, however, Jay observers were as successful as Jay cachers, whereas Nutcracker observers did no better than chance. So it seems that, whereas the Nutcracker is highly adapted for remembering where it hid its own seed, the gregarious Mexican Jay is more adept than the Nutcracker at remembering, and so exploiting, the caches of other birds.

caching: storing

questionGroups.bodyHtml:
Questions 1–4

The text has seven paragraphs, A–G. Which paragraph contains the following information?

Paragraphs

1 a comparison between learning in rats and learning in humans

2 an explanation of what initially prompted a research project

3 an overview of research into learning behaviour in animals

4 an analysis of cost-effectiveness

A. Paragraph A
B. Paragraph B
C. Paragraph C
D. Paragraph D
E. Paragraph E
F. Paragraph F
G. Paragraph G

Questions 5–9

Choose TRUE if the statement agrees with the information given in the text, choose FALSE if the statement contradicts the information, or choose NOT GIVEN if there is no information on this.

5 The purpose of the field trip to Israel was to investigate the feeding habits of the black rat.

6 Pine cones are the main source of food for forest rats in Israel.

7 The forest rats in Israel had a fixed method of peeling pine cones.

8 Forest rats know instinctively how to peel pine cones.

9 In extracting pine seeds from the cones, rats use only a small proportion of the energy they gain from eating them.

Questions 10–13

Complete the summary using the list of words. Choose the correct answer and move it into the gap.

Clark’s Nutcracker and the Mexican Jay

10 Clark’s Nutcracker and the Mexican Jay are two species of bird which store seeds in various places for use in winter. The Jay relies on this habit, and is more in its feeding habits. During an experiment, one bird stored seeds while another . Of the two species, the was consistently more able to find seeds which had been stored by other birds.

A. equally
B. Nutcracker
C. dependent
D. watched
E. solitary
F. observer
G. less
H. social
I. Jay
J. more

meta.title: Learning by example 动物学习

items.text:
题目翻译：对大鼠学习与人类学习的比较。
答案：D
解析：D段将两种学习过程并列：城市黑鼠得到预先剥去第一圈鳞片的松果后，能学会继续剥；人看到复印机如何开机后，也能推断后续用法。rather as 引出了黑鼠与人类学习的比较，因此选 D。
定位：D段
Further elegant experiments showed that naive adult urban rats can develop the skill if they are provided with cones from which the first complete spiral of scales have been removed, rather as people can deduce how to use a new photocopier once they have been shown how to switch it on. In the case of forest rats, mothers supply their infants with cones which they have partially stripped, thereby providing the key for acquiring the complete stripping skill.
原文翻译：后续一些设计巧妙的实验表明，如果给没有相关经验的成年城市黑鼠提供已经剥去第一整圈螺旋鳞片的松果，它们就能掌握这项技能；这很像别人演示了新复印机如何开机后，人们便能推断出该怎样使用它。森林母鼠会把自己剥开一部分的松果交给幼鼠，从而提供掌握完整剥松果技能的关键线索。

题目翻译：解释最初是什么促成了一项研究。
答案：B
解析：B段先交代学校实地考察的背景，接着说人们发现许多被剥至中心的松果，然后用 So 引出后续调查。研究最初就是为了解释这一发现，查明取食者及其取食方法，对应 initially prompted，所以选 B。
定位：B段
One of these papers starts with an account of a school field trip to Israel. In a pine forest there, many pine cones were discovered which had been stripped to the central core. So an investigation was started which had no weighty theoretical intent, but was directed initially at finding out what were eating the nutritious pine seeds, and how they managed to get them out of the cones.
原文翻译：其中一篇论文以一次学校赴以色列（Israel）的实地考察经历开篇。人们在那里的一片松林中发现了许多被剥得只剩中心芯轴的松果。于是，一项调查开始了；它并没有宏大的理论目标，起初只是想弄清楚，是什么动物在吃这些营养丰富的松子，以及它们如何把松子从松果中取出来。

题目翻译：对动物学习行为研究的概述。
答案：A
解析：A段从 Pavlov 的经典模型谈起，再提到操作性条件作用，最后转向近年来的社会学习研究。这是在概括动物学习研究的发展，而非介绍某一个具体实验，因此选 A。
定位：A段
The best known model of animal learning behaviour is probably the so-called classical model associated with the Russian scientist Pavlov. The key features of this model are stimulus, outcome and repetition. Pavlov demonstrated that animals could be trained to associate a sensory stimulus with a particular outcome, even where no natural association exists. In one famous experiment, dogs learned to associate the sound of a bell with the expectation of food. Subsequent models, such as the ‘operant conditioning’ model, also involved observing animals in isolation. Recently, however, behavioural research has focused on how animals are equipped to learn in social settings. And interest in the concept of role modelling, already a popular notion for guiding child development, has spread to other species.
原文翻译：最为人熟知的动物学习行为模型，可能是与俄罗斯科学家 Pavlov 联系在一起的所谓经典模型。这一模型的关键要素是刺激、结果和重复。Pavlov 证明，通过训练，可以使动物把某种感官刺激与特定结果联系起来，即使两者本来并无自然联系。在一个著名实验中，狗学会了把铃声与即将获得食物的预期联系起来。后来的模型，例如“操作性条件作用”模型，也是在动物被单独隔离的情况下对它们进行观察。不过，近年来的行为研究已将重点转向：动物具备怎样的能力，能够在社会环境中学习。以榜样示范来引导儿童发展的观念早已流行，如今，人们对这一概念的兴趣也延伸到了其他物种。

题目翻译：对成本效益的分析。
答案：E
解析：E段先问剥松果在能量上是否划算，再比较操作耗能与松子带来的能量收益，最后得出耗能不足收益10%的结果。投入与收益的比较正是 cost-effectiveness 分析，因此选 E。
定位：E段
The researchers went on to determine this by measuring the oxygen uptake of a rat stripping a cone. The rat was placed in a metabolic chamber so that the amount of energy used in the cone-stripping operation could be calculated. This was then compared with the energy benefit of the pine seeds, as measured by a machine known as a calorimeter. The rat's energy expenditure proved to be less than 10% of the energetic value of the cone – an acceptable profit margin.
原文翻译：研究人员接着测量黑鼠剥松果时的耗氧量，以此回答这个问题。他们把黑鼠放进代谢室，这样就能计算剥松果这一操作消耗的能量。再将这一能耗与松子所提供的能量收益相比较；后者用一种叫作量热计的仪器测量。结果表明，黑鼠消耗的能量不到松果所含能量的10%，这样的收益可以接受。

items.text:
题目翻译：赴以色列实地考察的目的是研究黑鼠的取食习惯。
答案：FALSE
解析：B段的叙述顺序是：学校实地考察时发现被剥开的松果，随后由 So 引出调查，起初要查明是什么动物在取食，最后才确认是黑鼠。题干把后来启动的调查写成了这次实地考察的既定目的；按这一因果顺序，本题选 FALSE。原文没有另行交代这次学校考察原本的具体目的。
定位：B段
One of these papers starts with an account of a school field trip to Israel. In a pine forest there, many pine cones were discovered which had been stripped to the central core. So an investigation was started which had no weighty theoretical intent, but was directed initially at finding out what were eating the nutritious pine seeds, and how they managed to get them out of the cones. The culprit proved to be the versatile and athletic black rat.
原文翻译：其中一篇论文以一次学校赴以色列（Israel）的实地考察经历开篇。人们在那里的一片松林中发现了许多被剥得只剩中心芯轴的松果。于是，一项调查开始了；它并没有宏大的理论目标，起初只是想弄清楚，是什么动物在吃这些营养丰富的松子，以及它们如何把松子从松果中取出来。结果发现，干这件事的是适应能力强、行动敏捷的黑鼠（black rat）。

题目翻译：松果是以色列森林黑鼠的主要食物来源。
答案：NOT GIVEN
解析：文中说明黑鼠会吃松子，也说明剥松果的能量收益较高，但没有比较松子与其他食物在它们饮食中所占的比例。会吃某种食物，不等于这种食物就是 main source（主要来源），因此为 NOT GIVEN。
定位：B段
In a pine forest there, many pine cones were discovered which had been stripped to the central core. So an investigation was started which had no weighty theoretical intent, but was directed initially at finding out what were eating the nutritious pine seeds, and how they managed to get them out of the cones. The culprit proved to be the versatile and athletic black rat. The forest-dwelling rat used a standard technique, biting off each cone scale in sequence, from base to tip, following the spiral growth pattern of the cone.
原文翻译：人们在那里的一片松林中发现了许多被剥得只剩中心芯轴的松果。于是，一项调查开始了；它并没有宏大的理论目标，起初只是想弄清楚，是什么动物在吃这些营养丰富的松子，以及它们如何把松子从松果中取出来。结果发现，干这件事的是适应能力强、行动敏捷的黑鼠（black rat）。这些生活在森林里的黑鼠采用一套固定方法，沿松果螺旋生长的方向，从底部到顶端依次咬掉每片鳞片。

题目翻译：以色列的森林黑鼠有一套固定的剥松果方法。
答案：TRUE
解析：原文说黑鼠采用 standard technique，并明确描述了从底到顶、沿螺旋顺序逐片剥除的步骤。这就是题干的 fixed method，与原文一致，因此为 TRUE。
定位：B段
The forest-dwelling rat used a standard technique, biting off each cone scale in sequence, from base to tip, following the spiral growth pattern of the cone.
原文翻译：这些生活在森林里的黑鼠采用一套固定方法，沿松果螺旋生长的方向，从底部到顶端依次咬掉每片鳞片。

题目翻译：森林黑鼠本能地知道如何剥松果。
答案：FALSE
解析：交叉寄养实验表明，幼鼠能否学会剥松果取决于抚养它们的母鼠；作者随后明确说这项技能 not inherited，而是 has to be taught。它需要学习，与题干 instinctively 所说的本能掌握相反，因此为 FALSE。
定位：C段
However, infants of urban mothers who were fostered to forest mothers acquired the skill, whereas infants of forest mothers fostered by urban mothers did not. Clearly, the skill is not inherited, but has to be taught.
原文翻译：然而，城市母鼠生下的幼鼠交由森林母鼠抚养后，学会了这项技能；森林母鼠生下的幼鼠交由城市母鼠抚养后，却没有学会。显然，这项技能并非遗传而来，而是必须通过传授才能掌握。

题目翻译：从松果中取出松子时，黑鼠消耗的能量，只占它们吃下松子所获得能量的一小部分。
答案：TRUE
解析：研究比较的是剥松果所消耗的能量与松子提供的能量收益，前者 less than 10% of 后者，确实只占一小部分，对应 small proportion，因此为 TRUE。不是说松子的营养价值低，而是获取它们的能量成本低。
定位：E段
This was then compared with the energy benefit of the pine seeds, as measured by a machine known as a calorimeter. The rat's energy expenditure proved to be less than 10% of the energetic value of the cone – an acceptable profit margin.
原文翻译：再将这一能耗与松子所提供的能量收益相比较；后者用一种叫作量热计的仪器测量。结果表明，黑鼠消耗的能量不到松果所含能量的10%，这样的收益可以接受。

The culprit proved to be the versatile and athletic black rat. The forest-dwelling rat used a standard technique, biting off each cone scale in sequence, from base to tip, following the spiral growth pattern of the cone.
原文翻译：人们在那里的一片松林中发现了许多被剥得只剩中心芯轴的松果。于是，一项调查开始了；它并没有宏大的理论目标，起初只是想弄清楚，是什么动物在吃这些营养丰富的松子，以及它们如何把松子从松果中取出来。结果发现，干这件事的是适应能力强、行动敏捷的黑鼠（black rat）。这些生活在森林里的黑鼠采用一套固定方法，沿松果螺旋生长的方向，从底部到顶端依次咬掉每片鳞片。

题目翻译：以色列的森林黑鼠有一套固定的剥松果方法。
答案：TRUE
解析：原文说黑鼠采用 standard technique，并明确描述了从底到顶、沿螺旋顺序逐片剥除的步骤。这就是题干的 fixed method，与原文一致，因此为 TRUE。
定位：B段
The forest-dwelling rat used a standard technique, biting off each cone scale in sequence, from base to tip, following the spiral growth pattern of the cone.
原文翻译：这些生活在森林里的黑鼠采用一套固定方法，沿松果螺旋生长的方向，从底部到顶端依次咬掉每片鳞片。

题目翻译：森林黑鼠本能地知道如何剥松果。
答案：FALSE
解析：交叉寄养实验表明，幼鼠能否学会剥松果取决于抚养它们的母鼠；作者随后明确说这项技能 not inherited，而是 has to be taught。它需要学习，与题干 instinctively 所说的本能掌握相反，因此为 FALSE。
定位：C段
However, infants of urban mothers who were fostered to forest mothers acquired the skill, whereas infants of forest mothers fostered by urban mothers did not. Clearly, the skill is not inherited, but has to be taught.
原文翻译：然而，城市母鼠生下的幼鼠交由森林母鼠抚养后，学会了这项技能；森林母鼠生下的幼鼠交由城市母鼠抚养后，却没有学会。显然，这项技能并非遗传而来，而是必须通过传授才能掌握。

题目翻译：从松果中取出松子时，黑鼠消耗的能量，只占它们吃下松子所获得能量的一小部分。
答案：TRUE
解析：研究比较的是剥松果所消耗的能量与松子提供的能量收益，前者 less than 10% of 后者，确实只占一小部分，对应 small proportion，因此为 TRUE。不是说松子的营养价值低，而是获取它们的能量成本低。
定位：E段
This was then compared with the energy benefit of the pine seeds, as measured by a machine known as a calorimeter. The rat's energy expenditure proved to be less than 10% of the energetic value of the cone – an acceptable profit margin.
原文翻译：再将这一能耗与松子所提供的能量收益相比较；后者用一种叫作量热计的仪器测量。结果表明，黑鼠消耗的能量不到松果所含能量的10%，这样的收益可以接受。

items.text:
题目翻译：Jay 对储藏食物这一习惯的依赖______。
答案：G
解析：F段说 Mexican Jay 虽然也储食，但 not nearly as dependent on this as the Nutcracker，即远没有 Nutcracker 那么依赖这一习惯。因此 relies 后填 less（较少），选 G；equally 和 more 分别表示同样多、更多，都与比较方向不符。
定位：F段
The Mexican Jay also caches food, but is not nearly as dependent on this as the Nutcracker.
原文翻译：Mexican Jay 也会储藏食物，但它对此的依赖远不及 Nutcracker。

题目翻译：Jay 的觅食习惯更______。
答案：H
解析：原文将两种鸟对照：Nutcracker 较独居，Jay 则 forages in social groups（成群觅食）。因此填 social（群体性的），选 H。solitary 恰好是另一种鸟的特点，不能移到 Jay 身上。
定位：F段
The two species also differ in their social structure, the Nutcracker being rather solitary, while the Jay forages in social groups.
原文翻译：这两种鸟的社会结构也不同：Nutcracker 比较独居，而 Jay 则成群觅食。

题目翻译：实验中，一只鸟储藏种子，另一只则______。
答案：D
解析：G段实验中，一只鸟藏食，另一只停在笼中观察。题干把被动表达 watched by an observer bird 改为 another watched，因此选 D。observer 是“观察者”这一名词，不能在 another 后充当这里所需的过去式谓语。
定位：G段
The design of the experiment is slightly comical, with a cacher bird wandering about a room with lots of holes in the floor and hiding food in some of them, while watched by an observer bird perched in a cage.
原文翻译：实验设计略带几分滑稽：一只负责藏食的鸟在地板上有许多洞的房间里走动，把食物藏进其中一些洞里；与此同时，一只停在笼中的鸟在旁观察。

题目翻译：在这两种鸟中，______一直更能找到其他鸟储藏的种子。
答案：I
解析：实验中，Jay 观察者找到种子的表现与 Jay 藏食者一样好，而 Nutcracker 观察者并不优于随机水平；结论又明确说 Mexican Jay 更擅长记住并利用其他鸟的藏食点。因此选 I，Jay。不要把 Nutcracker 善于记住自己的藏食点，误当成善于找到其他鸟储藏的种子。
定位：G段
More surprisingly, however, Jay observers were as successful as Jay cachers, whereas Nutcracker observers did no better than chance. So it seems that, whereas the Nutcracker is highly adapted for remembering where it hid its own seed, the gregarious Mexican Jay is more adept than the Nutcracker at remembering, and so exploiting, the caches of other birds.
原文翻译：然而，更令人惊讶的是，Jay 观察者与 Jay 藏食者一样成功，而 Nutcracker 观察者的表现却并不优于随机水平。由此看来，Nutcracker 非常适于记住自己藏种子的位置，而喜群居的 Mexican Jay 则比 Nutcracker 更善于记住其他鸟的藏食地点，并加以利用。
